title: The Divine Liturgy
hookLine: the liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom, sung almost entirely

cards: An old chronicle of Kyiv tells a story about where the faith of its people began. Their prince, the story goes, sent envoys to see how other peoples worshiped.
In Constantinople they were taken into the great church of Holy Wisdom on a feast day. Lamps. Gold.
Incense rising. Voices answering each other across the church. Back home, the chronicle says, their report was simple: they didn't know whether they had been in heaven or on earth.
They only knew that God dwelt there among people. It's a story, told long after. But it names what the liturgy itself is reaching for.

teach.b: First, the name. In the Byzantine churches, Catholic and Orthodox, the usual Sunday service is the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom, a bishop of Constantinople remembered for his preaching.
Chrysostom was a nickname: golden-mouthed. It's the Byzantine Mass, the same Eucharist, the same bread and wine, in another shape. Second, the singing.
Almost nothing in it is simply spoken. The priest sings, the deacon sings, and the people or the choir sing back.

teach.h: SUNG, NOT SPOKEN: LORD, HAVE MERCY.
teach.b: The deacon calls out petitions, for peace, for the sick, for travelers, for the city, and after each one comes the answer: Lord, have mercy. Again and again, like waves. Third, the Cherubic Hymn.

As the bread and wine are carried in procession, the choir sings that the people, in a mystery, stand in for the cherubim, the angels around God's throne, and asks them to lay aside all earthly cares to receive the King of all.
Later the people sing the song Isaiah heard in his vision, in the Douay-Rheims: "Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts, all the earth is full of his glory." The Latin Mass sings it too.
And the Second Vatican Council taught that the earthly liturgy is a foretaste of the liturgy of heaven, joined to it.
That's what the envoys were trying to say: in the Divine Liturgy, earth borrows heaven's song for a while, and the bills and the group chats wait outside.

how: Byzantine Catholics, like Orthodox Christians, celebrate the Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom on most Sundays; it is sung throughout, with the people or a choir answering the priest and deacon.

games.q: the Divine Liturgy — tap the pairs.

s: the Divine Liturgy is a different sacrament from the Mass

in the Divine Liturgy almost everything is sung

games.q: you're standing in the church as the bread and wine are carried in procession, and the choir sings the Cherubic Hymn. what does the hymn ask of you?
games.why: the people stand in for the cherubim, and lay aside all earthly cares to receive the King of all.

practice: If you have a recording of Byzantine chant nearby, let it play quietly; if not, the quiet will do.
Pick one earthly care, the loudest one, and imagine setting it down by the door like a bag you'll pick up later, not solving it, just setting it down.
If you pray, join the angels' song from Isaiah, holy, holy, holy, the Lord God of hosts; if not, simply listen, with nothing in your hands.
